test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 6 Sept 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: The sides of a rectangular field are 77 m and 50 m long. Its area is equal to the area of a circular field. What is the perimeter (in m) of the circular field? (Take π = \frac{{22}}{7})
solution:
**Given:**

Length of the rectangular field = 77 m

Breadth of the rectangular field = 50 m

Area of the rectangular field = Area of the circular field

π=227π=227 \pi = \frac{22}{7}

**Formula Used:**

Area of rectangle = Length × Breadth

Area of circle = πr2πr2 \pi r²

Perimeter of circle = 2πrπr \pi r

**Calculation:**

Area of rectangular field = 77 × 50

Area of rectangular field = 3850 m²

Area of circular field = 3850 m²

πr2πr2 \pi r² = 3850

227r2227r2 \frac{22}{7} r² = 3850

⇒ r2=3850×722r2=3850×722 r² = \frac{3850 × 7}{22}

⇒ r2=1225r2=1225 r² = 1225

⇒ r=√1225r=1225−−−−√ r = \sqrt{1225}

⇒ r=35r=35 r = 35

Perimeter of circular field = 2πrπr \pi r

Perimeter of circular field = 2 × 227227 \frac{22}{7} × 35

⇒ Perimeter of circular field = 2 × 5 × 22

⇒ Perimeter of circular field = 220 m

**The perimeter of the circular field is 220 m.**
